primary_meaning: Spiritual freedom from bondage to sin, death, and the Mosaic law through Christ

alternatives.meaning: Typological release from physical captivity or debt slavery (Jubilee/messianic liberation) pointing to spiritual freedom
Socio-political or national liberation applied to contemporary oppression
basis: liberation-theology readings of Isaiah and Luke

alternatives.meaning: Moral license or freedom to indulge the flesh

notes: New Testament usage of eleutheria/eleutheros consistently centers on Christ-won spiritual freedom; OT precedents function mainly as types. Political applications exist in some traditions but remain secondary to the spiritual sense in standard biblical interpretation.
